Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

shout verb and noun

also yell, cry out, call out, bawl, scream, a shout, shouting, don’t shout

classical

Plaut. Men. 1114b: Quid clāmās? quīn tacēs?
Ter. Ad. 728: Nōn clāmās? nōn īnsānis?

clāmō, clāmāre, clāmāvī, clāmātum

verb, first conjugation; intransitive, or with what is shouted

shout, cry out

The everyday word, of people, and in comedy even of snoring; also of geese and crickets (Lewis & Short). With an object it is to call out something, or call on someone: clāmāre aliquem.

Other words

  • clāmor, clāmōris m. — a shout, shouting

    noun, third declension · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 874: ut nē clāmōrem hīc faciās

    A shout or the noise of shouting: clāmōrem facere, to shout, make a row.

  • exclāmō, exclāmāre, exclāmāvī, exclāmātum — cry out, exclaim

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.56 (Lewis & Short): in stadiō cursōrēs exclāmant quam maximē possunt

    A single cry, or a sudden remark; also of a crowd applauding (Lewis & Short).

  • vōciferor, vōciferārī, vōciferātus sum — bawl, shout loudly

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.39 (Lewis & Short): vōciferārī palam

    Loud, often angry shouting, as of a man raising an outcry.

Examples

  • Quid clāmās? quīn tacēs?

    What are you shouting for? Why don’t you keep quiet?Plaut. Men. 1114b

  • Sciō tē bonā esse vōce, nē clāmā nimis.

    I know you have a good voice; don’t shout so much.Plaut. Most. 576

  • Nē clāmā: petītō hāsce ā mē decem.

    Don’t shout: ask me for these ten.Ter. Phorm. 664b

See also noisy, be quiet, cry, wail, speak up.

SourcesLewis & Short: clamo · Lewis & Short: clamor · Lewis & Short: exclamo · Lewis & Short: vociferor
